Umbrella for how this garden documents authenticating to GitHub: personal access tokens, OAuth scopes used by GitHub/CLI, and related how-tos.
GitHub/Auth/Personal — classic PAT (deprecated in favor of fine-grained)
GitHub/Auth/Personal/Fine-Grained — fine-grained PAT (repository + permission checkboxes; not the same strings as OAuth scopes)
GitHub/Auth/OAuth — what OAuth scopes are, normalization, inspection
GitHub/Auth/OAuth/Scope — catalog of scope names (workflow, repo:status, …) used by gh auth refresh -s
GitHub/CLI/How to create a Fine Grained Personal Access Token — create a fine-grained PAT (no gh subcommand today)

OAuth scopes are named permission groups an OAuth app (including GitHub/CLI during gh auth login) can request. Scopes limit what a token can do; they do not grant rights beyond what the authenticated user already has.
Distinct from GitHub/Auth/Personal/Fine-Grained permissions and from permissions: on GITHUB_TOKEN in GitHub/Action workflows.
Requesting multiple scopes may be stored as a normalized list: subscopes implied by a broader scope are dropped (e.g. user,gist,user:email → user, gist because user:email is included in user).
REST headers: X-OAuth-Scopes (granted) and X-Accepted-OAuth-Scopes (required for the endpoint) on API responses.
gh: gh auth status shows active account and scopes for stored credentials.
Login: gh auth login establishes credentials (browser/device flow).
Add scopes: gh auth refresh -h github.com -s <scope>[,<scope>…] — opens browser to authorize additional scopes; without -s, maintains existing scopes.
Remove: gh auth refresh --remove-scopes <scope>… — idempotent; cannot remove minimum set repo, read:org, gist.
Reset: gh auth refresh --reset-scopes — back to default minimum for the auth flow.
Fine-grained PAT — per-repo permission matrix; see GitHub/Auth/Personal/Fine-Grained.
GitHub App — fine-grained permissions instead of classic OAuth scopes (GitHub’s recommended direction for new integrations).
GitHub/Auth/OAuth/Scope — one page per documented scope name

Reference index for OAuth scope names used by GitHub/CLI (gh auth refresh -s), classic PATs, and OAuth apps. Official descriptions live on the linked docs page; each scope below has a local leaf with gh notes and cross-links.
Cannot be removed via gh auth refresh --remove-scopes: GitHub/Auth/OAuth/Scope/repo, GitHub/Auth/OAuth/Scope/read:org, GitHub/Auth/OAuth/Scope/gist
(no scope) — read-only access to public information (profile, public repos, gists). No separate leaf page; used when an app does not request scopes (e.g. some CLI device flows).

Official description: Fully manage GPG keys.
Request: gh auth refresh -h github.com -s admin:gpg_key
Official description: Fully manage the organization and its teams, projects, and memberships.
Request: gh auth refresh -h github.com -s admin:org
Official description: Grants read, write, ping, and delete access to organization hooks (OAuth tokens only on hooks created by the same OAuth app).
Request: gh auth refresh -h github.com -s admin:org_hook
Official description: Fully manage public keys.
Request: gh auth refresh -h github.com -s admin:public_key
Official description: Grants read, write, ping, and delete access to repository hooks; use to limit access to hooks only (repo / public_repo already include hooks).
Request: gh auth refresh -h github.com -s admin:repo_hook
Official description: Grants the ability to create and manage codespaces (may expose a GITHUB_TOKEN with different scopes).
Request: gh auth refresh -h github.com -s codespace
Official description: Grants access to delete packages from GitHub Packages.
Request: gh auth refresh -h github.com -s delete:packages
Official description: Grants access to delete adminable repositories.
Request: gh auth refresh -h github.com -s delete_repo
Official description: Grants write access to gists.
Request: gh auth refresh -h github.com -s gist (usually already present after login)
gh gist create and other gist write operations
Part of the default minimum scope set for GitHub/CLI stored credentials
Related: GitHub/CLI/How to/Create a Gist on GitHub from the command line, GitHub/Auth/OAuth
Official description: Grants read access to notifications; mark-as-read; watch/unwatch repositories; read, write, and delete thread subscriptions.
Request: gh auth refresh -h github.com -s notifications
Official description: Grants read/write access to user and organization projects.
Request: gh auth refresh -h github.com -s project
Official description: Limits access to public repositories: code, commit statuses, projects, collaborators, deployment statuses; required to star public repositories.
Request: gh auth refresh -h github.com -s public_repo
Official description: Read audit log data.
Request: gh auth refresh -h github.com -s read:audit_log
Official description: List and view details for GPG keys.
Request: gh auth refresh -h github.com -s read:gpg_key
Official description: Read-only access to organization membership, organization projects, and team membership.
Request: gh auth refresh -h github.com -s read:org (usually already present after login)
Listing organizations and teams visible to the authenticated user
gh commands that resolve org context without needing GitHub/Auth/OAuth/Scope/write:org or GitHub/Auth/OAuth/Scope/admin:org
Official description: Grants access to download or install packages from GitHub Packages.
Request: gh auth refresh -h github.com -s read:packages
Official description: Grants read-only access to user and organization projects.
Request: gh auth refresh -h github.com -s read:project
